title: Smashed Cucumber Salad
subtitle: Chinese-style smashed cucumbers with garlic, chilli and rice vinegar
excerpt: Cucumbers smashed with the flat of a knife, salted to draw out water, then dressed in garlic, rice vinegar, sesame oil and a little chilli. The smashing breaks the flesh so the dressing penetrates all the way through.
sourceNotes: Smashed cucumber salad (pai huang gua) is a classic of Chinese home cooking, found across multiple regional cuisines. The technique of smashing rather than slicing cucumber is documented in Chinese cookbooks throughout the 20th century and has been widely adopted in contemporary Western cooking. The dressing, based on rice vinegar, garlic and sesame oil, follows the Sichuan and northern Chinese flavour profile.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made 15 to 30 minutes before serving. The cucumber holds well for up to 2 hours with the dressing on; after that it continues to release water.

content.text: Smashed cucumber has a completely different character to sliced cucumber. The rough, irregular surface created by smashing absorbs a dressing all the way through the flesh, rather than just coating the outer surface. Salting after smashing draws out the water that would otherwise dilute the dressing. Use the sesame oil sparingly; it is strong and a little overwhelms quickly.

Cut the cucumber in half lengthways. Place the halves cut-side down on the board and smash firmly with the flat side of a large knife or a rolling pin until the flesh cracks and breaks apart. Cut into rough 3 cm chunks. Toss with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt in a colander. Leave to drain for 15 minutes, then pat dry with kitchen paper.

Stir together {{garlic}} of crushed garlic, {{rice-vinegar}} of rice vinegar, {{soy-sauce-light}} of light soy sauce, {{sesame-oil}} of toasted sesame oil, {{rapeseed-oil}} of rapeseed oil, {{caster-sugar}} of sugar and chilli flakes if using. Toss the drained cucumber in the dressing and transfer to a serving bowl. Scatter over the {{sesame-seeds}} of toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately or leave for up to 2 hours.

items.symptom: Salad is watery and the dressing is diluted
items.cause: Cucumber not salted and drained long enough.
items.fix: Salt the cucumber for a full 15 minutes, shake the colander, and press with kitchen paper before dressing. The expelled liquid is what waters the dressing.

items.cause: Rice vinegar varies in acidity between brands.
items.fix: Add the extra half teaspoon of sugar and a tiny extra pinch of salt. The balance of sweet, salty, sour and umami is what makes the dressing work.

content.text: Smashed cucumber salad came from Chinese home cooking into the British repertoire through a wave of interest in Chinese regional food from around 2015. The technique is simple, the ingredients are easy to source, and the result beats any sliced cucumber dish. It works alongside Chinese meals, grilled meats, tofu or rice.
